prompt: Create ONE square PNG contact sheet containing exactly nine AAC communication pictograms in a precise 3 by 3 grid of equal square cells. White background, thin pale-gray grid dividers at exactly one-third and two-thirds of the canvas. No writing, letters, numbers, captions or watermark. Large clear simple friendly flat pictograms with dark navy outlines and restrained colours, consistent scale, generous white margins inside each cell. Meaning must not rely on colour alone. Intended for Russian-speaking children who may not read. Row 1 LEFT TO RIGHT: YES — large affirmative check mark inside a circle; NO — large X inside a circle; I WANT — friendly child reaching an open hand toward a toy ball. Row 2: I DO NOT WANT — same child turning away from that ball with a raised refusal palm; HELP ME — larger helping hand supporting a smaller reaching hand; IT HURTS — concerned but not frightened child touching an upper arm, a small pain burst at that spot. Row 3: DRINK — clear cup of water close to a mouth; TOILET — simple side-view toilet, no person; ENOUGH / STOP — a large raised open palm inside a stop-shaped outline. Each symbol stays wholly inside its own cell. Do not add additional panels or decorative elements. This is a pictogram design prototype, not a clinical recommendation.

Create ONE new square PNG sheet of nine AAC pictograms in a precise equal 3x3 grid. Use the reference ONLY for consistent flat style, dark navy outlines, white background, thin light gray dividers, the same friendly brown-haired blue-shirt child, generous margins and simple large forms. Replace all reference symbols with the following NEW meanings, in exact row-major order. No text, letters, numbers, captions, watermarks or extra panels. Row1: MORE — two hands with fingertips meeting, small inward motion marks, a clear request for more; EAT — child bringing a spoon of food from a bowl to the mouth; REST — child seated comfortably and relaxed in an armchair, hands on lap, no bed. Row2: UNCOMFORTABLE — child shifting awkwardly on a chair, uncomfortable posture and frown, no pain star; GOOD / FEEL WELL — happy relaxed child giving thumbs up; BAD / FEEL UNWELL — child with sad tired face giving thumbs down, no injury. Distinguish each meaning visually, not by colour alone. Exactly nine full symbols, centered inside equal cells with safe white margins.
